title: Tobacco market
questionText: The diagram shows a tax imposed on tobacco. What is the size of the tobacco tax per packet?
explanation: The per-unit tax is the vertical distance between the original supply curve and the S+tax curve — $4 per packet.

title: Tobacco market
questionText: Consider the same tax. What is the total government revenue raised from this tax?
explanation: Government revenue is the tax per unit times the quantity sold after the tax: $4 x 40 = $160.

title: Tobacco market
questionText: What is the producer revenue following the introduction of the tax?
explanation: Producer revenue is the price producers keep (after handing over the tax) times the quantity sold: $8 x 40 = $320.

title: Tobacco market
questionText: How much of the tax revenue is paid by the consumer?
explanation: The consumer's share is the rise in the price they pay times the quantity: a $2 rise x 40 packets = $80.

title: Tobacco market
questionText: By how much has overall spending on tobacco reduced with the imposition of the tax?
explanation: Consumer spending falls from $10 x 50 = $500 before the tax to $12 x 40 = $480 after — a reduction of $20.

title: Market for solar panels
questionText: A government decides to subsidise solar panels. Which of the following best describes the positive externality of solar panels?
answers: The solar panel owner has lower electricity bills
The wider community benefits from reduced air pollution
The government spends money to subsidise the solar panel
Firms benefit from increased profits due to higher demand for solar panels
explanation: The positive externality is the benefit to third parties — cleaner air for the wider community — not the private savings of the owner or the firm's profit.

title: Market for solar panels
questionText: What is the size of the solar panel subsidy per panel?
explanation: The per-unit subsidy is the vertical distance between the original supply curve and the subsidised supply curve — $20 per panel.

title: Market for solar panels
questionText: What is the total government spending on the solar panel subsidy?
explanation: Government spending is the subsidy per unit times the quantity sold after the subsidy, which the diagram gives as $120.

title: Market for solar panels
questionText: What is the total producer revenue after the subsidy?
explanation: Producer revenue is the price producers receive (the consumer price plus the subsidy) times the quantity sold — $3,600,000.
